Mastering Webinars SOP
FICTIONAL TRAINING MATERIAL FOR TESTS

The seven segment webinar
Every webinar follows the same seven segments. The timings below are for a sixty-five minute webinar.
Segment 1: Hook and promise, five minutes. Say exactly what they will walk away with.
Segment 2: Origin and credibility, seven minutes. Tell the story of how the method was found. Keep it about them, not you.
Segment 3: The big mistake, ten minutes. Name the mistake most of the audience is making right now.
Segment 4: The new mechanism, fifteen minutes. Teach the method that replaces the mistake.
Segment 5: Proof framework, ten minutes. Show how to check the method works. Only use real, verified results with permission.
Segment 6: The offer, twelve minutes. Explain what is included, who it is for and who it is not for.
Segment 7: Questions and close, six minutes. Answer real questions from the chat and restate the offer.

Running the chat
Ask the audience to type a word in the chat in the first two minutes. This wakes up the room.
Ask one engagement question per segment.
Answer real questions from real attendees. Never plant questions or invent attendees.

The offer moment
Before the offer, ask permission: "Would it be useful if I showed you how we can help you do this?"
State the price once, clearly, then explain the value.
If there is a real deadline, say what it is and why it exists.

Show-up and replay sequences
Send a registration confirmation straight away with the date, the time and the link.
Send reminders one day before, one hour before and as the webinar goes live.
Send the replay within two hours of the webinar ending. Keep the replay up for forty-eight hours and explain why it comes down.

Hand-off to sales
Anyone who asks a question about the offer gets a DM from a setter within one hour.
Anyone who watched more than half the replay gets a follow-up message the next morning.
